subject: Media Arts
title: Y7-8 Media Arts — Performance Cycle
progression_endpoint: Students investigate how media arts concepts construct representations across cultures and contexts, design and structure media works with clear intent, apply production processes to make works with responsible practice, and present to audiences.
_parallel_strands: D strand (skills development and reflection) runs throughout the performance cycle as a parallel capability strand — not included in the sequential phases. Same pattern as Science Inquiry in Waypoints Planner and DT algorithm/tracing strands. A future swimlane view will display D strand as a parallel lane alongside the sequential phases.

phases.label: Exploring
phases.checkpoint: Students can investigate how media arts concepts construct representations across cultures and contexts, and engage with First Nations media arts and ICIP rights.

width_tiers.minimum_width: Investigate at least one arts work from a specified cultural, historical or contextual source; identify how arts concepts are used; explain what ICIP rights mean and give one example of respectful engagement.
width_tiers.typical_width: Investigate arts works across at least two cultural or historical contexts; analyse how context shapes artistic choices; investigate First Nations arts practices from multiple regional contexts; connect investigation to own practice decisions.
wider: Investigate First Nations arts works that cross multiple artforms and analyse how they produce layered meaning
Research the social, cultural and historical developments that shaped a specific style or tradition
Connect investigation to specific practice decisions — distinguish informed adaptation from imitation

phases.label: Conceiving
phases.checkpoint: Students can design and structure a media arts work using pre-production tools, with deliberate media language choices connected to intended meaning and audience.

width_tiers.minimum_width: Generate initial artistic material or ideas through improvisation, brainstorming or design; select and develop material using at least one arts-specific device or convention with deliberate intent.
width_tiers.typical_width: Generate material using multiple strategies; develop and select material across multiple devices, conventions or structural forms; justify choices in relation to intended meaning for a specific audience or context.
wider: Generate material through investigation of existing works across cultural contexts; develop a distinctively personal approach informed by but not derivative of those works
Use Viewpoints or similar questioning methods to push ideation beyond familiar territory
Trial multiple structural or compositional approaches and evaluate each against intended meaning

phases.label: Making
phases.checkpoint: Students can apply production processes and media arts concepts to produce a work that communicates intended meaning with responsible media practice throughout.

width_tiers.minimum_width: Produce an arts work applying arts concepts and techniques deliberately; use at least one piece of feedback to make a documented refinement.
width_tiers.typical_width: Produce a complete arts work where concept, technique and material choices consistently serve intended meaning; evaluate and refine through multiple feedback cycles; document how the work developed.
wider: Present or perform the work for an audience and iterate based on their response
Evaluate whether the work successfully communicates the intended meaning and identify specific aspects that would change in a future version
Apply responsible arts practice (ICIP, copyright, attribution) throughout production

phases.label: Presenting
phases.checkpoint: Students can present media arts works using responsible media practices, considering audience relationships and evaluating how presentation choices shape reception.

waypoints.note: Applying culturally responsive approaches — ICIP protocols applied to own work before presenting publicly.

width_tiers.minimum_width: Apply ICIP responsibilities before sharing; present or perform the work for an audience using appropriate skills and conventions; reflect on whether the presentation communicated the intended meaning.
width_tiers.typical_width: Apply responsible arts practice throughout presentation; make deliberate presentation decisions about context, audience relationship and curation; evaluate the gap between intended and received meaning; identify specific improvements.
wider: Present in multiple contexts and compare how audience reception differs
Collect and evaluate audience feedback systematically; develop criteria for evaluating presentation effectiveness
Reflect on how respectful relationships and cultural responsiveness were expressed and interpreted by the audience
